en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses in the Philippines.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, features a distinctive shaggy crest of dark brown feathers on its head.
The Legislative branch of the Philippine government is composed of the Senate and the House of Representatives.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of Luzon over 2,000 years ago.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian to study at Harvard Medical School and invented a bamboo incubator.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white flower, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a two-beat step dance mimicking a river's current.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system that uses characters to represent syllables rather than individual letters.
Every Filipino citizen who is at least eighteen years old and registered has the right to vote.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the Bonifacio Monument in Caloocan and the Oblation statue at the University of the Philippines.
Intramuros is the historic walled city in Manila built by the Spanish to serve as the seat of government.
